title: feat(isolation): pluggable secret providers — Infisical runtime injection (docker substrate)
body:
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider-design.md` (read the **Re-integration addendum** and **Test Plan** at the end)
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider/`
Run: `docs/superpowers/runs/2026-09-14-feat-secrets-injection.yaml` (adopted, fr-goal@1; parked on the manual phase 6)
Resumes: #333

## Summary

Makes secret resolution in `fr.isolation` pluggable behind a `SecretProvider` seam. `env-file`, the default, keeps today's ambient model unchanged. `infisical` fetches secrets at runtime, on demand, inside the devcontainer: `fr isolation exec --secret KEY -- cmd`. Version **4.12.0 → 4.13.0**: a minor bump for the new flag, provider and scaffold options.

This PR was opened in June against fr 3.3 and sat blocked on the cluster (#333). It was rebased onto main 4.3.0 (98 commits), re-integrated, and put through three review rounds. It has since been rebased twice more to keep up with main: onto 4.5.2 on 2026-09-19 and onto **4.12.0 on 2026-09-21**. Both rebases give a linear history with no merge commit.

## What changed since the June version

- **Rebased onto the 4.x isolation targets.** main split isolation into devcontainer, host-worktree and external targets. The June wiring conflicted with that split, so the rebase took main's side of `local.py` / `isolation_cmd.py`. A new TDD phase (5) then rebuilt the wiring on the devcontainer target, with the carried June wiring tests as its RED.
- **`--secret` is devcontainer-only.** In host-worktree and external modes it refuses with an actionable error and runs nothing (operator decision).
- **Per-exec tokens in a per-workspace, contained, read-only-mounted directory:**
  - Each secret-bearing exec writes its own `O_EXCL` `0600` token file under `~/.cache/fr/run-tokens/<repo>/<profile>/<workspace>/` (`0700`).
  - That directory is bind-mounted **read-only** at `/run/fr-secrets`.
  - The wrapper reads the token, then runs `infisical run … -- env -u INFISICAL_TOKEN -- "$@"`, so the user command never sees it.
  - `post_exec` removes that exec's file, whether the command returned or raised.
- **The host follows the committed mount, and the path is contained.**
  - The token directory is parsed from `devcontainer.json`'s `--mount`, as the env-file provider has done since #272.
  - fr refuses any source that isn't exactly three levels under `~/.cache/fr/run-tokens`, or that contains `..`, a symlink or an unresolved variable.
  - Truncation never follows a symlink or blocks on a FIFO the container could plant (`O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`).
- **Teardown and gc:**
  - Token cleanup runs after the container is verified gone (the #354 guarantees are intact).
  - It still runs when the profile config is unreadable.
  - gc's orphan paths also reap token directories, only once the container is confirmed gone.
- **The env-file ensure follows post-#408 main:** a legacy vk mount raises, and files are hardened to `0600`/`0700`.
- **The scaffold composes with the multi-backend `--backend/--host` options:** base install, then forge CLI, then Infisical CLI.
  - `--secret-provider` is validated.
  - `--infisical-*` flags are rejected with env-file.
  - Re-scaffolding to infisical warns about a leftover plaintext env-file.
- **Docs and artifacts:** skill docs rewritten within the 120-line cap; OpenCode/Hermes mirrors regenerated; the plan's `fr_version` migrated and floored to `>=3.7.0,<5.0.0`.

## Security invariants (tested)

- App-secret values never touch host disk. The only host artifact is a short-TTL token in a per-exec `0600` file, removed after its command.
- No secret material on any argv, host or container. The client secret goes via env at mint, the token via the mounted file, and no `--remote-env` is added.
- On demand: no `--secret` means no mint and no profile read. An undeclared key fails before mint, and the CLI exits 2.
- Every interpolated `fr-profiles.yaml` value is `shlex.quote`d, since that file is PR-reachable. Infisical config is validated before minting.
- Back-compat: a profile with no `secret_provider` behaves exactly as before.

## Review findings & fixes

All findings are recorded in `docs/superpowers/journals/plans/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider.md`, each with its proving tests.

**June review (phases 1–4), re-checked after the rebase:**
- C1: shell injection via unquoted `project_id`/`env`/`path`. Fixed and carried over.
- C2: the token lingered until `down`. The Target `try/finally` was lost in the rebase and rebuilt in phase 5.
- I1: token cleanup was skipped when the profile config was unreadable. Lost in the rebase, rebuilt.
- I2: an exec could carry `--remote-env`. Rebuilt.
- I3: the CLI install swallowed stderr. Fixed and carried over.
- M1: a mint error could leak stdout. Fixed and carried over.

**Phase-5 review, round 1** (all fixed except one refutation):
- I1: the token directory was shared by every workspace of a profile.
- I2: the host token directory didn't follow the mount.
- I3: a token leaked when `exec_wrap` raised after minting.
- m1: plain exec read the profile.
- m2: cleanup ran before teardown was verified.
- m3: gc orphan paths skipped token cleanup.
- m4: mint had no timeout or empty-token check.
- m5: the user command inherited `INFISICAL_TOKEN`.
- m6: kubernetes-auth read a never-written file.
- m7: scaffold flags weren't validated.
- m8: a leftover env-file got no warning.
- m9: stale prose.
- m10: a constant lived in the wrong module.
- **Refuted — m8 (second half), pin the Infisical CLI install like glab/tea:** Infisical publishes no checksummed static artifact for its apt bootstrap. Its apt repo signing key is the trust anchor, and a code comment marks this as a known v1 limitation.

**Round 2** (containment verification, all fixed):
- V1: the mount source had no containment.
- V2: the gc orphan glob was unguarded.
- V3: label-orphan tokens were reaped before the container was confirmed gone.
- V4: the kubernetes-auth mount directory wasn't created.
- V5: a partial token write leaked.
- V6: `env --` was missing, so a leading `NAME=VALUE` or `-x` user argument was parsed by `env`.
- V7: `${localEnv:VAR:default}` wasn't parsed.
- V8: no test proved `down` follows a non-canonical mount.

**Round 3** (all fixed):
- W1: a symlink or FIFO planted by the container could be followed on truncate. Fixed with the read-only mount plus `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`.
- W2: `..` was collapsed instead of rejected.
- W3: set-but-empty variables should take the default.
- W4: one bad match aborted the gc token reap.
- W5: a vacuous test assertion.

## Decisions

**Operator Q&A (2026-09-14):**
- `--secret` is devcontainer-mode only.
- The live Infisical smoke stays with the operator.
- Rebase and force-push to this PR.
- Hard-tier phases ran on Fable 5.1.

**Process:**
- The Target wiring was rebuilt as a new TDD phase instead of hand-splicing the conflicts.
- Phase 1 carries no walking-skeleton marker: it shipped in June, before the convention existed.

**Known limitations** (in the spec addendum):
- Custom `--path` workspaces that share a basename share a token directory.
- The gc fallback misses orphan token directories of a clone renamed after scaffolding.

**Accepted residual:** a check-then-`rmtree` TOCTOU at teardown, after the container is verified gone.

**Unconfirmed:** the devcontainer CLI's handling of `${localEnv:VAR:default}` for a set-but-empty variable. fr uses `||` semantics. The CLI source wasn't available to check, and the phase-6 smoke pins it. A mismatch fails loudly at `devcontainer up`.

## ⏳ Phase 6: manual and **unimplemented; the operator pushes to this PR**

1. In Infisical (the frank `infisical` namespace), create a **Universal-Auth** machine identity that is **read-only** to the project/path, and set a **short Access-Token TTL** on the identity.
2. On the host, export `FR_INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID` / `FR_INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET` and install the `infisical` CLI. Universal-auth mints host-side.
3. Scaffold an infisical profile, run `fr isolation up` in devcontainer mode, then run the Test Plan item 6 checks below.
4. Record the result with `fr plan edit docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-15-infisical-secret-provider --complete-phase 6 --note "…"`, flip `secret-provider-live-infisical-smoke` to `skipped`, then `fr run resolve 2026-09-14-feat-secrets-injection --step implement-phase --item phase/6 --state done`.

## Test Plan (post-merge, operator-driven)

Every item runs without a live Infisical except item 6. Item numbers match the acceptance-matrix rows listed in brackets.

1. **Back-compat default** [`secret-provider-envfile-default`]. A profile with no `secret_provider` resolves to `EnvFileProvider`. `up_prepare` creates the mounted env-file at `0600` and refuses a legacy vk mount. `exec_wrap` returns an empty wrap.
2. **Scaffold** [`secret-provider-scaffold-infisical`]. `fr init scaffold --secret-provider infisical` writes the `infisical:` block with the default auth env-var names, omits `--env-file`, mounts the token directory, appends the CLI install after any forge-CLI install, and prints the TTL reminder. An env-file profile is unchanged.
3. **On-demand injection** [`secret-provider-infisical-on-demand`]. On the devcontainer target, `exec --secret KEY` puts `infisical run --projectId … --env … --path … --` ahead of the user command and keeps the command intact at the tail. Without `--secret`, nothing is minted and nothing is wrapped. An undeclared key raises before any mint, and the CLI exits 2 having run nothing.
4. **Nothing secret on argv; tokens are per-exec** [`secret-provider-no-secret-on-argv`]. The minted token and the UA client secret appear in no assembled argv (host mint or `devcontainer exec`), and no `--remote-env` is added. Two wraps produce two distinct `0600` token files. `post_exec` removes the file for its own exec, whether the command returned or raised. `down` runs `cleanup`.
5. **Mode scope** [`secret-provider-mode-scope`]. `HostWorktreeTarget.exec` and `ExternalTarget.exec` with non-empty `keys` raise `IsolationError` naming devcontainer mode and run nothing. With empty `keys` they behave as before. The CLI maps the refusal to exit 2.
6. **Live smoke, operator-driven** [`secret-provider-live-infisical-smoke`]. With a real read-only, short-TTL Universal-Auth identity and the two host env vars set: `fr isolation exec --secret KEY -- printenv KEY` prints the value; the same command without `--secret` prints nothing; `INFISICAL_TOKEN` is absent in the child (`exec --secret KEY -- sh -c 'printenv INFISICAL_TOKEN'` prints nothing); and the workspace's token directory is empty afterwards.

## Acceptance

`fr acceptance check`: 112 rows OK (ci 93 / skipped 14 / not-implemented 5).

Rows added since `origin/main`, each with its defense:
- `secret-provider-envfile-default` (**ci**): pins the back-compat promise that every existing profile relies on.
- `secret-provider-scaffold-infisical` (**ci**): the only way an operator creates an infisical profile, so its shape must not drift.
- `secret-provider-infisical-on-demand` (**ci**): the feature's core promise, that secrets are fetched only when asked for.
- `secret-provider-no-secret-on-argv` (**ci**): the security invariant the design depends on, ps-visible argv and per-exec tokens.
- `secret-provider-mode-scope` (**ci**): pins the operator's devcontainer-only decision, so `--secret` can't silently run unwrapped on a pod.
- `secret-provider-live-infisical-smoke` (**not-implemented**): needs a real Infisical identity, so it is operator-owned phase 6 and can't run in CI.

The existing repo-wide debt (14 skipped, 4 other not-implemented rows) is unchanged by this PR.

## Verification

**GitHub CI is the authoritative run.**

**Rebased onto `origin/main` at 4.12.0 on 2026-09-21** (33 commits, linear), after main landed the unit-record run model (#508), isolation reap guards (#507), OpenCode phase-executor and tier dispatch (#495, #504, #506) and the executor-handoff bounds (#514). Beyond the replay:
- **The previous 4.6.0 bump was dropped** and replaced by one bump from main's tip to 4.13.0.
- **Reconciled against main afterwards.** The rebase took this branch's side on generated and append-structured files so it could keep moving, and each one was then rebuilt from main:
  - `matrix.yaml`: main's file plus the six `secret-provider-*` rows (177 rows).
  - `fr-init` and `fr-isolation` SKILL.md: main's versions, including the gh-486 host wording and status line v2, with the Infisical and `--secret` edits re-applied, at exactly 120 lines each. Only these two skills and their mirrors differ from main.
  - The OpenCode and Hermes mirrors and all three acceptance reports were regenerated.
- **Run cursor migrated** through main's new hops, including the 4 → 5 unit-record rewrite. `fr run status` reads it back cleanly.
- **Privacy check:** this branch's spec, plan, journals, run file, matrix rows and PR body contain no third-party identifiers (per the new third-party-privacy rule).

Full local suite at the rebased head: **4052 passed, 85 skipped**. The one earlier failure, the unarchived-plans tripwire, cleared once the branch was rebased on #520. Ruff, format and mypy are clean. Other local checks at the rebased head: `fr validate artifacts` on all 53 artifacts, `fr acceptance check` with 177 rows OK, journal checks clean, plan self-review passes, and `fr harness parity --check` plus the skill tripwires pass.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Explainers:** the fr-goal explainer lists "Profile secrets → `~/.config/fr/secrets/<repo>/<profile>.env`". That stays true, because env-file is the default and Infisical is opt-in, so no explainer change is needed. `fr-isolation.html` has no committed source (a known gap) and doesn't describe secrets.
- **Unarchived-plans tripwire:** main was briefly red on three merged-but-unarchived plans. #520 archived them, and this branch is rebased on top of #520, so the tripwire passes here.

## Ready checklist

- [x] CI green on the 4.13.0 head `da0409c` (all checks pass, merge state CLEAN)
- [x] Taken out of draft by the operator
- [ ] Operator review of the 2026-09-21 rebase (a history rewrite after the earlier OK)

title: [derio-net/super-fr] super-fr chattiness — reporting contract, prose lint, opt-in STE style
body:
> **Draft — do not merge.** Ready checklist (all three must hold before this becomes ready):
> - [ ] CI green
> - [ ] Explicit review OK from the operator
> - [ ] No commits since that OK

## Summary

super-fr is too chatty. This PR changes what super-fr itself controls: its skills and its own artifact checks. It does not put a tone prompt in front of every session.

The first version of this PR forced a Simplified Technical English (STE) output style and installed a global rule. Review showed that this reached every session, needed exceptions for other skills (blog-craft, for example) and for Claude Code settings, and stayed non-deterministic. The spec was revised in place (decisions d6–d10), and phases 5–8 implement the revision on the same branch.

- **Reporting contract.** fr-goal and fr-debugging speak to the operator only at gates, blocks and delivery. Each update is the result in 1–3 lines, then the next step. Evidence goes to the journal and the PR body.
- **Short, not obscure (d11).** The same contract adds: "Short means split, not packed: plain words, name what an id refers to, keep the \"because\"." Without it, the length cap pushes toward packed, jargon-dense updates, and the plain-word rules reach only operators who select the STE style.
- **Row tables.** fr-brainstorming and fr-acceptance present new acceptance rows as one table (`id | claim | level | defense`), not a paragraph each.
- **Prose lint, warn only.** New `fr.prose_lint`: sentences over 25 words, and filler words. `fr journal add` prints at most five warnings, one line each, labelled `title:` or `body:`. `fr plan self-review` prints one line per source, with two excerpts and a count. No exit code changes (d9). The lint strips code, embeds, quotes, tables and front matter first, so it does not fire on paths, fences or wrapped code spans.
- **Opt-in STE style.** `plugins/super-fr/output-styles/simplified-technical-english.md` stays, without `force-for-plugin`. You select it in `/config`.
- **Removed.** The `ste-output-tone` rule and all its wiring (install.sh, OpenCode mirror, Hermes SOUL block, AGENTS.md), and the phase-executor STE line. None of it was released.
- **Release: 4.18.0.** `main` reached 4.17.1 while this branch was open; the branch merges it and takes the next minor.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-ste-output-tone-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-ste-output-tone/` (phases 1–4 built the first version; phases 5–8 are the revision)

## Baseline (spec §2)

11 recent super-fr sessions: 68% of assistant words in end-of-turn replies, 31% narration next to tool calls, 2% Insight blocks, about 23 words per tool call. The transcripts miss the harness "user hasn't heard from you" nudges, so the numbers are indicative. The post-merge Test Plan re-measures with the same script (spec Appendix A).

## Fixed along the way

- **Version clashes that would have failed CI.** `main` released 4.4.0, 4.5.0 and later 4.14.x while this branch was open, overtaking every number this branch had taken. The branch now takes 4.18.0.
- **Two broken tests, fixed twice.** This branch fixed a pinned fr-version ceiling (`<4.5.0`) and a non-hermetic marketplace-clone test; `main` fixed both independently. The merge takes `main`'s versions.

## Merged main (4.12.0, 4.14.3, then 4.17.1)

`main` moved three times during review. The branch merges it both times (merge commits, so every per-phase commit and the SHAs the journal cites stay intact). The first merge (4.12.0):

- **Generated files** (version manifests, `uv.lock`, skill mirrors, acceptance reports) took `main`'s side and were regenerated.
- **fr-goal** took `main`'s text and re-applied the reporting contract and the row table — still 120 lines.
- **`fr journal add`** is create-only on `main` now (gh-429); the prose-lint warning is re-added to the new `add`, and its tests follow: a duplicate id exits 2, and plan-scope entries need `--phase` or `--global`.
- **Matrix** merged by row id: `main`'s 171 rows plus this PR's 5.
- **Run cursor** migrated to schema 5 with `fr migrate artifacts --yes`.
- **Explainer** citations shifted by the three contract lines; the page was regenerated with `--isolated` after a byte-parity check against `main`'s page.

The second merge (4.14.3) had one real conflict: `main` fixed the same Rich-markup bug in the self-review print (#428) with `escape()`. The merge keeps `main`'s fix and adds `soft_wrap`, so each issue stays on one line. Every other overlapping file merged by itself and was checked: fr-goal still 120 lines with the contract once, the journal hook once, the matrix without duplicates. The explainer page was regenerated from the merged source again.

The third merge (4.17.1, fifteen commits) conflicted only in version manifests, `uv.lock` and the three reports: `main`'s side, then the bump and a regeneration. It also fixes one explainer citation the first remap missed (`:42-53` → `:45-56`, line 104), found by checking every range against `main`'s shifted by the three contract lines.

## Not in this PR

- PR body sections and skill announce lines stay (d8).
- The `fr` CLI and hook messages keep their wording (d1).
- No shipped rule reaches OpenCode outside this repo, because no installer copies `.opencode/instructions`. This PR ships no rule, so it no longer depends on that gap.

## Explainers currency

`docs/explainers/01-fr-goal.md:519` says the agent "presents these rows and a short defense for each". The table keeps a defense column, so the sentence stays true. No explainer describes mid-run updates or output styles, so no explainer prose changes. `01-fr-goal.md` does change: its fr-goal line citations shift by the three contract lines, and the page is regenerated with `--isolated` after a byte-parity check against `main`'s page.

## Acceptance

`fr acceptance check`: **210 rows OK** — ci 179, skipped 24, not-implemented 7, failing 0 (after merging `main`). The three committed reports are in sync.

### Rows added by this PR (`fr acceptance check --added-since origin/main`)

| Row | Status | Defense |
|---|---|---|
| `ste-style-opt-in` | skipped | The operator can select the STE style, and super-fr forces nothing. A unit test pins the frontmatter without `force-for-plugin`; the `/config` selection is the post-merge walk (Test Plan step 2). |
| `fr-goal-reports-result-and-next-step` | skipped | The operator's stated complaint, stated as an outcome — now including plain words (d11). A unit test pins the skill text; live behaviour, plainness and the re-measure are the post-merge walk (Test Plan steps 3–4). No code detects obscurity, so step 3 is a human read. |
| `acceptance-rows-presented-as-table` | skipped | New rows must reach the operator as one table, not a paragraph each. A unit test pins the skill text; whether an agent obeys it is the post-merge walk (Test Plan step 3). |
| `journal-add-warns-on-long-prose` | ci | The lint must nudge without failing anything. `test_prose_lint.py` and `test_journal_add_prose_warning.py` run in CI; Test Plan step 5 is owed post-merge. |
| `plan-self-review-warns-on-long-prose` | ci | Same claim for plans and specs. `test_prose_lint.py` and `test_self_review_prose.py` run in CI. |

The three rows of the first version (`ste-style-forced-in-claude-code`, `ste-rule-reaches-every-harness`, `ste-insight-blocks-kept-short`) are retired: they were born on this branch, were never merged, and describe the forced style this PR removes.

### Other matrix edit

`hermes-rules-soul-block` names four shipped rules again, which is what ships after the `ste-output-tone` rule is removed. Its status and levels are unchanged.

### Open acceptance debt (not this PR)

The 7 `not-implemented` rows and the other `skipped` rows predate this branch and belong to other specs.

## Review findings, fixes and refutations

Every phase was reviewed; each finding is recorded in the plan journal (`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-14-ste-output-tone`).

<details><summary>Findings (fixed / refuted)</summary>

### r2-m5-progressive · finding [refuted] · M5 progressive tense excluded: refuted (phase 2)

Reviewer suggested allowing the present progressive for work in progress. Refuted: ASD-STE100 excludes the progressive, and the operator asked for the standard. 'The test runs in the background' is a valid STE status line.

### r2-m8-loader · finding [refuted] · M8 marker comments in style body: no action (phase 2)

Reviewer confirmed the frontmatter shape is valid and the ste-shared HTML comments reach the system prompt as a few literal tokens with no harm. No change needed.

### r2-i1-one-block · finding [refuted] · I1 optional 'one Insight block per reply': not adopted (phase 2)

Reviewer offered an optional rule limiting Insight blocks to one per reply. Not adopted: operator decision d3 is to keep the Insight blocks. The fix cancels only the length permission.

### r2-i1-insight · finding [fixed] · I1 Insight override cancelled a limit that did not exist (phase 2)

Old text: 'does not permit replies longer than these rules permit' — the rules set no reply-length limit. Fix: name the hook's permission ('exceed typical length constraints'), state 'Insight blocks do not make a reply longer', and 'These rules take precedence over that prompt'. Test pins all three phrases.

### r2-i2-scope · finding [fixed] · I2 Scope wider than d1 (phase 2)

Old: 'all text that you write for a person' covered code comments, docs, specs, CLI strings; conflicts with explainers-currency voice. Fix: closed list (replies, status updates, skill announcements, PR bodies, journal entries, subagent results) plus 'Do not apply them to files that you edit: code, comments, docs, specs, plans, or CLI and hook messages.' Spec §5.A updated. Test pins the exclusion.

### r2-i3-formats · finding [fixed] · I3 No precedence for prescribed formats (phase 2)

Skills prescribe announcements and verbatim blocks; callers prescribe report layouts. Fix: 'If the operator, a skill or a caller gives a format or exact words, use them. Write your own sentences in STE.' Spec §5.A updated. Test pins it.

### r2-i4-length · finding [fixed] · I4 Text broke its own 20-word instruction limit; guard was prose (phase 2)

The Scope instruction had 23 words; journal 173c595e7078 wrongly checked it against the 25-word description limit and recorded 'no change needed' — that entry is superseded by this one. Fix: sentence rewritten (longest shared sentence now 19 words, checked by reader). Added test_no_shared_sentence_exceeds_the_description_limit (25-word guard in code) and test_sentence_splitter_finds_a_long_sentence (the guard can fail). The 20-word instruction limit stays a reader check: a test cannot tell instructions from descriptions (spec §5.E.7).

### r2-m1-filler-failopen · finding [fixed] · M1 Filler test failed open on unbalanced quotes and line wraps (phase 2)

Fix: normalize whitespace; assert balanced double quotes.

### r2-m2-filler-list · finding [fixed] · M2 FILLER tuple duplicated the Words list (phase 2)

Fix: the test parses the filler list from the Words bullet and asserts it contains just/really/i think.

### r2-m3-markers-headings · finding [fixed] · M3 Marker order unchecked; headings matched as substrings (phase 2)

Fix: _shared_block asserts START precedes END; section headings match as exact lines (re.M). _section normalizes whitespace so wrapped phrases match.

### r2-m4-instruction-two-meanings · finding [fixed] · M4 'instruction' used with two meanings (phase 2)

Fix: the Insight section says 'another prompt'; 'instruction' now only means a sentence type.

### r2-m6-code-spans · finding [fixed] · M6 Commands counted toward the word limit (phase 2)

Fix: 'Put commands and paths in code spans. Do not count them as words.' The sentence splitter drops code spans.

### r2-m7-licence-wording · finding [fixed] · M7 One sentence close to ASD rule wording (phase 2)

Fix: 'Write one instruction in each sentence' reworded to 'Give only one instruction in a sentence.'

### r3-i1-opencode-consumers · finding [fixed] · I1 OpenCode instructions never reach consumer machines (phase 3)

Verified: scripts/install.sh (lines 535-558) copies OpenCode skills and commands only; no installer delivers .opencode/instructions, so the rule loads in OpenCode only inside this repo (opencode.json). Pre-existing gap, affects every shipped rule. Fixed by narrowing the claim: spec §2, §3 and the §8 row now say OpenCode gets the rule only inside this repo; phase 4 narrows the matrix row text before any status flip. Consumer delivery is listed as a follow-up in the PR body.

### r3-m2-token-cost · finding [fixed] · M2 Token cost understated (phase 3)

Main thread loads both carriers (style ~400 words + rule ~460 words), ~1,100 input tokens, not 600. Spec §6 corrected.

### r3-m3-rule-header-paths · finding [fixed] · M3 Rule header named repo paths in every session (phase 3)

The globally installed rule header named plugins/ and docs/superpowers/ paths that do not exist in consumer repos. Header cut to: plugin also sends this text as an output style; output styles do not reach subagents or other harnesses; licence note.

### r3-m4-commit-messages · finding [fixed] · M4 Commit messages neither in nor out of scope (phase 3)

Added 'Do not apply them to commit messages.' to both carriers (consistent with d1 and spec-review R1), spec §5.A updated. TDD: scope test asserted it first (1 failed, 9 passed), then green.

### r3-m5-identity-strip · finding [fixed] · M5 Identity test compared stripped blocks (phase 3)

Added _raw_block: the identity test compares the unstripped bytes between the markers, after the marker count/order checks.

**CI on `d52e0e6`** (run 35839889874): every check passes — lint, typecheck, test, validate-artifacts, matrix, opencode-plugin-test, version-sync, version-bump-required. The `test` job: **4598 passed, 91 skipped in 228.61s (0:03:48)**. The PR is mergeable with no conflicts.

Local checks, with the worktree's own `uv run fr`, all exit 0: both mirror syncs, `bump-version --check` (4.18.0 on every surface), `fr acceptance check` (210 rows, 0 failing), `fr acceptance report --deterministic`, `fr validate artifacts`, and ruff. The full local suite on the third merge commit (`6ce8093`, before the d11 commit): **4599 passed, 88 skipped**. After the d11 commit, the targeted suite (reporting contract, skill validation, both skill-mirror tripwires, tool neutrality, acceptance) passes, and `fr plan self-review` reports no prose issues in this spec.

Plan: 8 of 8 phases complete, 44 of 44 steps ticked. Every phase was reviewed by a separate reviewer; each finding is fixed, or refuted with a reason in the plan journal. d11 came after delivery, from an operator question. It is one TDD commit (test red, then green) plus a spec amendment, recorded as spec-journal decision `d11-short-not-obscure`. It is not a plan phase.

### Requirements checklist (spec §5, re-checked after all three merges)

- §5.A the reporting contract and the d11 clarity sentence are in fr-goal (120 lines) and fr-debugging (120 lines).
- §5.B fr-brainstorming, fr-acceptance and fr-goal present rows as one table; no skill asks for a defense per row.
- §5.C `fr.prose_lint`; `fr journal add` warns on new entries (a duplicate id is refused before any lint); `fr plan self-review` prints one line per source, escaped and soft-wrapped.
- §5.D the output style is opt-in.
- §5.E the rule and all its wiring are gone.
- §5.F all five test files exist and run in CI.
- §5.G version 4.18.0.

## Decisions

From the two batched Q&A rounds (spec §4; journal `docs/superpowers/journals/specs/2026-09-14-ste-output-tone.md`):

**2026-09-14**

- **d1 — Scope:** agent replies and skill-prescribed text; CLI and hook messages out of scope.
- **d2 — Activation:** forced style plus a shipped rule. *Superseded by d7.*
- **d3 — Explanatory plugin:** keep the Insight blocks, in STE, with no longer replies. This now applies only when you select the STE style.
- **d4 — Test Plan:** operator walk after merge, plus CI tests.
- **d5 — No dictionary** (agent decision, forced by the ASD licence): paraphrased principles only.

**2026-09-15**

- **d6 — Reframe:** the chattiness problem first. The skill audit and the artifact lint are prerequisites, not follow-ups. Revise the spec and extend the plan in place.
- **d7 — Repurpose:** remove the rule, its wiring and `force-for-plugin`; keep the STE style as opt-in.
- **d8 — Skill audit:** remove mid-run status reports and per-row presentation. Keep PR body sections and announce lines.
- **d9 — Lint:** warn only, in `fr journal add` and `fr plan self-review`.
- **d10 — Measure and reports:** record the baseline, re-measure after merge, and make each operator update the result then the next step.

## Test Plan

### Pre-merge (CI)

The tests in spec §5.F, the existing skill-validation, drift and install tests, and `fr validate artifacts`.

### Post-merge — operator-driven

1. Update the plugin: `claude plugin update super-fr@derio-net--super-fr`.
   Restart Claude Code.
2. In `/config`, make sure that "Output style" is not forced to "Simplified
   Technical English". Select it once, send one message, and examine the reply.
   Then select your normal style again.
3. Run `/fr-goal` on a small goal. Make sure that the agent speaks only at the
   Q&A, at a block or failure, and at delivery. Make sure that each update is
   the result, then the next step. Make sure that it reads plainly: no
   unexplained ids or jargon, and each decision keeps its reason. When it
   presents new acceptance rows, make sure that they arrive as one table, not a
   paragraph for each row.
4. Run Appendix A over that session. Compare words per tool call and the
   end-of-turn share with the baseline in §2.
5. In any fr repo, run `fr journal add --scope spec --slug <any> --kind
   discovery --title x --body '<a 30-word sentence>'`. Make sure that a warning prints and the exit code is 0.
6. If a check fails, record the reply text or the output in a follow-up issue.

title: docs: Codex harness adapter — spec and plan (design only, nothing implemented)
body:
**Design only. Nothing is implemented.** This PR carries the spec, the 6-phase plan, the journals and five `not-implemented` acceptance rows for a Codex harness track. It is a draft on purpose: the design is up for review before any of it gets built.

super-fr supports Claude Code, OpenCode and Hermes Agent. Codex gets no skills install, no rule delivery and no isolation gate. This plans the fourth track.

## Why now

Two observed failures, not a hypothesis:

1. A Codex session in `derio-net/willikins` (PR #405) built a "Codex compatibility" layer while knowing nothing about fr: it edited the base clone of an fr-enabled repo, wrote a v1 flat plan, and put review reports in an ad-hoc `docs/reviews/`. Every one of those is a rule super-fr already ships to three other harnesses.
2. All eleven of the operator's `~/.codex/skills/fr-*` links were dangling (a retired `marketplaces/` path). Codex had fr skill entries it could not read.

## Verified this session

Empirically, with `codex debug prompt-input` (an offline prompt render — no API calls, no live agent session), on codex-cli 0.153.4:

- `$CODEX_HOME/skills` **is** scanned, though the official build-skills page omits it. OpenAI's own bundled `skill-installer` defaults there too.
- Repo-level `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is discovered, with no git repo required.
- Absolute symlinks are followed.
- **A dangling skill symlink is skipped silently**: exit 0, empty stderr, the good skill still lists, the broken one is simply absent. There is no error to notice, which is why the operator's links stayed broken — and why the plan ships a doctor rather than a one-time relink.
- The four shipped rules total 13,066 bytes; a full-inline block would be 13,129, and with super-fr's own 16,365-byte `AGENTS.md` that is 90% of the 32 KiB `project_doc_max_bytes` cap. Discovery *stops* at the cap, so an oversized block would silently evict a consuming repo's own instructions. Hence: rule bodies install as files, and the `AGENTS.md` block is a pointer, test-enforced at ≤ 2 KiB.

From official docs, **not** observed live: the PreToolUse payload fields, `tool_name: apply_patch` even when the matcher says `Edit`/`Write`, the deny shapes, and that trust is recorded against a hook's **hash** — so a super-fr upgrade that edits a hook leaves the gate inert until re-trusted. Assumed and flagged: the exact `tool_input.command` encoding for `apply_patch`; the planned parser keys off the `*** … File:` markers so either form works.

**No Codex session has ever loaded or fired these hooks.** That needs a live session plus a manual `/hooks` trust grant, and it is the spec's post-merge Test Plan.

## The trap this plan exists to avoid

`fr_isolation_decide_edit()` returns **ALLOW for any non-absolute path**, by design. `apply_patch` paths are repo-relative. An entrypoint that forwards them verbatim allows *every* patch while every other test stays green. Phase 2 proves the fix can fail by removing it and watching the test go red. A patch is also atomic — any blocked path must deny the whole call — asserted in both file orders.

## Scope decisions

- Skills install to `$CODEX_HOME/skills/<name>`, repairing the existing broken links in place instead of creating a competing location.
- Hooks register at user level with absolute paths (the `fr hermes install` pattern). A project-level `.codex/hooks.json` needs a command-path base that could not be verified here, and only loads in a trusted project; it is documented as operator-owned rather than generated.
- **`fr codex install` defaults to a dry run**: it shows the diff and writes nothing, and an explicit flag performs the write. These are the operator's global, cross-project Codex files (journal `d12`).
- Deferred with reasons, not half-built: the merged-PR push guard, the SessionStart acceptance nag (needs a Codex context-injection shape nobody verified), and Codex phase dispatch in fr-goal (both `fr-goal` and `fr-isolation` SKILL.md are already exactly at the enforced 120-line cap).

One brief item was **refused**: a "fail-open when jq is absent" test would assert nothing, because the shared library resolves python3 first and jq only as a fallback. Replaced by two honest tests — the gate stays armed without jq, and refuses explicitly when no parser resolves at all (journal `d6`).

## State and resume

`fr plan self-review` passes, `fr validate artifacts` passes (21 artifacts), `fr acceptance check` exits 0. The five new rows are `not-implemented` by design; no test exists yet, and nothing is RED-verified.

To resume: `fr run advance 2026-09-16-feat-codex-harness-adapter`, then dispatch `super-fr:fr-phase-executor` serially, one phase at a time, **never** with `isolation: "worktree"`. Phase 6 owns the 4.5.0 minor bump, CHANGELOG, docs, and flipping the acceptance rows.

Consumer: derio-net/willikins#405, which states that Codex has no fr enforcement hook. That stays true until this ships.
